title: rhinanthus major var. serotinus
intro: Rhinanthus major var. serotinus, commonly known as Early Summer Rye Brome or late broomrape, is a parasitic flowering plant that belongs to the Orobanchaceae family. This plant has been traditionally used in folk medicine for its potential health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory and antiviral properties, and is believed to help in treating conditions such as fever, rheumatism, and cough. The therapeutic actions of Rhinanthus major var. serotinus include expectorant, diaphoretic, and anti-inflammatory effects, which may be attributed to its bioactive constituents, including alkaloids, glycosides, and phenolic compounds. However, further research is needed to confirm the efficacy and safety of this plant for medicinal use.
